## `things-cli` v0.8.0 — parity with the app's lists

Every list in Things.app now has a CLI view that returns the same rows in the same order, projects included. Until now a project scheduled for Today was visible in the app and absent from `things today`, so an agent driving the CLI never saw it. Every view was measured against the app's own lists by uuid, and every one of them now matches. Two JSON fields became words, listings are deterministic, agents are steered to UUIDs, and the code behind the views was reorganised so the next parity fix is one table entry. Two breaking changes, below.

### Breaking changes: `type` and `start` are strings

`type` and `start` on task rows in every `--json` output were Things' internal integers. They are now words, so a caller can tell a project from a task, or a deferred item from a scheduled one, without a lookup table. Anything matching on `type == 1` or `start == 2` must change. On input, the legacy integers are still accepted. `start` also appears on `things projects -j` rows. (#208, #214, #218, #223, #241, #251)

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| `"type": 0` | `"type": "task"` |
| `"type": 1` | `"type": "project"` |
| `"type": 2` | `"type": "heading"` (never returned by any command) |
| `"start": 0` | `"start": "inbox"` |
| `"start": 1` | `"start": "anytime"` (Today when it carries a date) |
| `"start": 2` | `"start": "someday"` (Upcoming when it carries a date) |

The word for a to-do is `task` everywhere the CLI speaks, in JSON values, error payloads, the agent brief and the docs. The one exception is the `things import` payload, which keeps Things' own spelling `to-do`. Run `things skill install` after upgrading so agents pick up the new skill, which documents all of this.

### Projects appear where the app shows them

- **today, upcoming, someday, logbook, trash and deadlines include projects.** A project scheduled, deferred, closed, trashed or due is a row with `"type": "project"` in JSON and a `(project)` marker in plain text. **anytime is the exception**, as in the app: it lists a project's tasks under the project as a group header rather than as a row. The bare `--area` and `--tag` listings include projects too; `--project X` never matches a project itself. (#201, #205, #206, #209, #212, #216, #213, #220, #217, #236, #222, #232)
- **logbook includes cancelled items**, with `status` telling them apart. (#210, #225)
- **logbook and trash fold a closed or trashed project's tasks into the project's row**, as the app does; the same fold applies under `--include-completed`. Ask for the project instead: `things --project <uuid>` on a closed project returns its tasks whatever their status, and `things show <uuid> --agent` lists them with their real status marks instead of claiming the project has no open tasks. Logbook went from 1334 rows to the app's 910 on the author's data, row for row. (#229, #235, #249, #252, #253, #260)
- **Closed items file by calendar day.** An item you close stays in Today and Anytime, struck through in the app, until midnight, then moves to the logbook. `things today --include-completed` and the new `things anytime --include-completed` show them until then; `--include-completed` used to keep everything closed since the last "Log Completed Now". (#230, #233, #238, #247)
- **someday no longer surfaces tasks that live inside a project.** The app keeps a deferred task inside its project, whichever list the project is in; measured with a probe project created and deleted through the app. `things someday --project X` is now rejected like the other impossible filters. (#211, #228)
- **Naming a trashed project with `--project <uuid>` reaches its contents in every view.** The app returns a trashed project's untrashed children when asked for them directly, and so does the CLI now, in today, anytime, logbook and the rest, not only in the bare `things --project` form. Trash keeps its fold, so a task trashed on its own account inside a later-trashed project stays where the app keeps it. (#263, #273)
- Repeating templates, headings and trashed items stay excluded from these views exactly as before.

### Listings are ordered as the app orders them, and deterministically

- **today, anytime and someday** arrange rows as the app does: unfiled items first, then areas in area order, and inside an area its own tasks before those of its projects. **upcoming** is ordered by start date. Closed items shown under `--include-completed` stay where they were rather than sinking to the end. (#217, #236, #237, #239)
- **Every view, search and lookup ordering ends in a total tiebreak**, so the same list run twice numbers the same items the same way and `things complete 3` acts on the row you read. Deadlines and logbook had no tiebreak at all. Numbers still move as items are added, closed or rescheduled. (#221, #226)

### Agents: use UUIDs, and `--json` no longer touches the row cache

- **A `--json` listing no longer writes the numbered-row cache.** JSON output never showed row numbers, so a JSON listing could only move the numbers a person had just read, and two agents on one machine could race each other into completing the wrong task. Numeric references keep resolving against the last plain-text listing. The bundled skill and https://things.rlew.io/agents/ now tell agents to use `--json` and act on `uuid`, never on row numbers, with every example resolving a UUID first. Thanks to @davidolrik for the report. (#246, #261)
- **`things skill install` honours each agent's config-directory variable**: `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` for Claude Code (thanks to @davidolrik for the fix), `$CODEX_HOME` for Codex and `$PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` for Pi, each with that tool's own rule for tilde expansion. (#227, #234, #250, #254)
- **`things projects -j` reports `start`, `startDate` and `deadline`**, and its `taskCount` and `openCount` are documented, with a recipe for finding projects with no open tasks and the caveats that go with it. (#202, #204, #203, #207)
- **References and filters match literally.** A task reference, a search query and the `--project`, `--area` and `--tag` filters used to be SQL LIKE patterns, so `things complete '20_30 review'` could resolve to and complete `20:30 review`, and `things search '50%'` matched everything. `%` and `_` are now characters to find. (#262, #266, #267, #268)
- **Row numbers expire after four hours.** The numbered-row cache now records when the listing ran and which command printed it, and a bare number against a listing older than four hours is refused with an error that names the listing to re-run, or the UUID to use instead, under the stable token `stale list cache`. A cache written by an older release counts as stale, so the first numeric reference after upgrading asks for a fresh listing. (#265, #271)
- **A title shared by a project and a task is an ambiguity, not a coin toss.** `things project edit Chores` used to resolve the first row with that title, land on the task and recommend a retry that edited the wrong item. An exact title that matches more than one open item now returns the existing `ambiguous task` error listing each candidate with its type and UUID, so the caller picks by UUID. (#194, #270)
- The jq `select` examples in the agent docs were missing `.[] |` and failed against the JSON array; all are fixed. (#225)

### Under the hood

Each list view is now described once, in one table, with a golden test that pins the exact SQL for every view, filter and flag combination; the four copies of the column renderer became one; `main.go` was split by command group; the `status`, `type` and `start` codecs share one implementation. None of this changes output: it was verified byte for byte against the previous binary across hundreds of live invocations. (#240, #242, #243, #248, #258, #259, #264)

### Also

- **`edit` and `project edit` refuse the wrong kind of reference** with the same structured error instead of opening a `things:///update` URL for the wrong kind of item. (#190, #193, #219, #231)
- **An empty listing that names a repeating project template says so.** `things --project <template>` prints a one-line note on stderr that the template's tasks are not listed, instead of an unexplained empty result. (#174, #272)
- The reference site at https://things.rlew.io moved to Hugo with a new landing page, an agents page, a social preview image and analytics, and rebuilds on each release. Local builds stamp version, commit and date. (#183, #185, #186, #188, #192, #195, #198)

### Requirements

macOS with Things3 installed. Binaries for Apple Silicon (`darwin_arm64`) and Intel (`darwin_amd64`).
